english.title: Driver / operator / manager fail to stop smoking in smoke-free vehicle used wholly / mainly for work - Wales
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the driver]_
(B)_[the operator]_
(C)_[a person concerned in the management]_

of a vehicle used wholly or mainly in the course of paid or voluntary work and

(D)_[by more than one person,]_
(E)_[to transport members of the public or a section of the public,]_

failed to take reasonable steps to cause a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), smoking in that vehicle to stop smoking
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 15(1) and (2) and 17 of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020 and sections 6(5)(c), (6) and (9) and 15 of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.

english.notes:
(i) Smoke-free vehicles are defined in regulation 15 of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020. Vehicles which are smoke-free because they are used in the course of paid or voluntary work are smoke-free all the time, for details see regulation 15(2) and (4).
(ii) Where the vehicle is not used wholly or mainly in the course of paid or voluntary work and by more than one person or to transport members or a section of the public, see H22455/PH17012; where it is used for private purposes and a child is present, see H22456/PH17013.
(iii) For a defence where the person did not know, and could not reasonably have been expected to know, that the person in question was smoking, see section 6(7) and (8) of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.
